title: You Become Like the Company You Keep
passage:
There was once a family of parrots. One day, the mother and father went out to look for food. They left their two babies alone. While the parents were gone, a cruel hunter appeared. The hunter caught the babies and dropped them in his bag. One of them got away. He flew as far as he could, and finally, he came to a church. Many monks lived there. They let the parrot stay, and they took care of him. The second parrot stayed with the hunter.

Both parrots grew up in their new homes. The monks' parrot learned many kind words from them. The cruel hunter's parrot only learned bad ones.

Then, one day, a traveler passed through. At the hunter's house, the parrot yelled and said bad things. That scared the traveler away. He hurried to the church. The parrot there greeted him politely.

“I saw another parrot near here, but he was so mean,” said the traveler.

The parrot said, “That was likely my brother. His owner is cruel, so he learned terrible language. However, my owners treated me kindly. We become like the company we keep.”
